summary: Partial roadmap with 388 declaration-sized nodes. Arbitrary-section rational-character LEFT coaction now has the explicit heterobasic coefficient square, identity/composition and unchanged-weight formulas, and one-way preservation of universal coinvariance. New conditional proof bodies are checked against incoming admitted coordinate/coaction contracts. All incoming source routes, general root-stack scope, nonreduced fibres and geometric/sheaf boundaries remain; no implementation or stage is certified closed. Separate native evidence proves the existing rational-character/infinite unity-root coordinate block; three computation lemmas expose natural representatives and factorial levels. No geometric or stage closure is asserted. The ten arbitrary-section rational LEFT coaction contracts now have separate admission-free exact-Mathlib proof evidence, and the ten coefficient contracts of PR5978 are replayed without their former admitted inputs. The defining-degree boundary and three additional tests are specified. Two inherited tensor-power precedence errors are corrected only in the Lean prototypes, leaving all mathematical contracts unchanged. Next complete full exact-pin Tau typing, positive-index/higher-universe transport, convolution-point identification, coherent root-object reindexing, affine Spec limits, fpqc frame torsors and quotient/DVR/Kummer comparisons. These algebraic certificates do not identify all coinvariants with A. Preserve all eight gaps, thirteen requests and both source routes. The actual finite coaction equalizer is identified with the coefficient algebra through diagonal/zero-row coordinates, uniformly in wild characteristic and with arbitrary nonreduced coefficients. The factorial arbitrary-section root algebra has the actual native coefficient invariant subalgebra A. Rational-character extraction and injective finite-stage inclusions supply a finite-level criterion, existence and uniqueness of the coefficient, and the native equalizer algebra equivalence, also for wild and nonreduced bases. This algebraic calculation does not discharge the geometric quotient, Spec-limit, root-groupoid or fpqc frame-descent contracts.

nodes.title: Tensor powers used by root objects
nodes.statement: For a native invertible sheaf M on a scheme T define M⁰=O_T and Mⁿ⁺¹=Mⁿ⊗M, with coherent transport of line-bundle isomorphisms. This is a root-object interface over the existing tensor operation, not a new definition of line bundles.

For a stack base, pull back to an atlas and descend with the same definition; do not replace the stack base by a coarse space.

nodes.title: Affine quotient presentation
nodes.statement: If X=Spec A and (L,s) is trivialized with s=f, then √[n]{(L,s)/X}≃[Spec AdjoinRoot(Tⁿ−f)/μ_n], with the diagonalizable action already constructed. This is a quotient stack with torsors, not an orbit set.
hypotheses: The exponent n is a positive integer; the scheme or stack base and all base changes use the stated fppf topology.
proofSteps: Use root-trivialization-equation and root-arrow-scalars on native trivializations: objects have unit u with u zⁿ=f and arrows have z_b=w z_a, u_b wⁿ=u_a. The generic quotient-stack/torsor construction remains SF.1; these scalar equations are its actual root-specific input.

Use the affine coaction and its laws. In trivial coordinates φ(eⁿ)=u with u a unit and section b e satisfying u bⁿ=f. Compatible normalized coframes e↦a form Spec A[a]/(aⁿ−u), which is the unit-parameter torsor by affine-torsor-unit-inverse and the imported finite-free/torsor criterion. The equivariant root-chart coordinate is x↦ab. It scales with weight one. Do not treat Spec A[x]/(xⁿ−f) as a torsor over Spec A at the branch locus.
On the torsor the root section is a function t satisfying tⁿ=f.
Conversely descend the trivial root line and function on an equivariant torsor; show the two operations inverse on objects and arrows.
acceptance: When f=0 the chart is Spec A[t]/tⁿ; its nilpotents remain present.

For s(x)=0 pass to the reduction t=0, then identify the residual classifying gerbe.
For s(x)≠0 the solution scheme is a μ_n-torsor and its quotient stack is the point.

nodes.title: Regularity and the tame DM condition
nodes.statement: If X is regular and D is a regular effective Cartier divisor, √[n]{(O(D),s_D)/X} is regular; when n is invertible on X it is Deligne–Mumford with μ_n inertia over D and trivial inertia outside D. If a geometric branch point has characteristic dividing n, its μ_n inertia is not étale, so the stack is not DM there. An empty divisor still gives X in every characteristic.
hypotheses: The exponent n is a positive integer; the scheme or stack base and all base changes use the stated fppf topology.
proofSteps: Locally choose a regular parameter f cutting out D; the equation tⁿ=f replaces that parameter and gives a regular chart.
For invertible n the finite diagonalizable stabilizer is étale; descend regularity through the atlas.
At an actual branch point use the computed μ_n inertia and its nonreduced characteristic-dividing part to obstruct the DM diagonal.
acceptance: On a DVR the n=2 root is regular in odd residue characteristic; the assertion is not that arbitrary sections cut regular divisors.

nodes.title: Infinite root stacks
nodes.statement: Define √[infinity]{(L,s)/X} as the two-inverse limit of the finite root stacks indexed by positive integers ordered by divisibility, on the fpqc scheme site. Its objects over T are compatible finite root objects with transition isomorphisms satisfying cocycles; arrows are compatible systems of root isomorphisms. It is an fpqc stack, hence also an fppf stack by restriction, and is not asserted to be an algebraic stack of finite presentation. Its affine quotient uses fpqc torsors.
hypotheses: All finite exponents are positive. Infinite root objects and quotient torsors use the fpqc scheme site.
proofSteps: Use the already planned compatible-family carrier, retaining objects, arrows and unit/composition equations.
Every finite root is an fpqc stack by root-fpqc-descent. Apply the imported limit-stack-descent theorem to those components and their finite transitions.

For a single effective Cartier divisor, TV17 Proposition3.5 identifies the compatible system with its logarithmic infinite root. The local quotient comparison is its separate infinite-affine-quotient leaf.
acceptance: A set-theoretic inverse limit of isomorphism classes discards coherent automorphism data and is insufficient.

nodes.title: The infinite reduced DVR fibre
nodes.statement: The reduced closed fibre of the infinite root of a DVR with residue field k is the inverse system of the root gerbes of the normal line, banded by lim_n μ_n=Ẑ(1). It is noncanonically equivalent to B_kẐ(1); a chosen trivialization of the normal line gives a compatible neutralization. The neutralization is not part of the canonical root stack.

A trivialization of that one-dimensional k-space supplies compatible trivial root objects at all n.
The automorphisms form lim μ_n, and coherent descent gives the banded gerbe; use the source’s reduced-fibre convention for the infinite limit.

nodes.title: Kummer classes of infinite-gerbe points
nodes.statement: After choosing a neutralization of the infinite reduced DVR gerbe over k, its k-points up to isomorphism identify with H1_fpqc(k,G), where G=lim_n μ_n, and with lim_n H1_fppf(k,μ_n)=lim_n k×/(k×)^n. Infinite torsors are fpqc; the finite Kummer calculation is fppf. The full groupoid retains G(k) automorphisms, and changing the neutralization changes the chosen origin.
hypotheses: A DVR with residue field k of arbitrary characteristic and a chosen compatible neutralization.
G is the fpqc inverse-limit sheaf of all μ_n, with power transition maps.
proofSteps: The neutralization identifies the reduced gerbe with fpqc G-torsors.
The Kummer torsor-limit comparison gives its actual finite tower, including the quotient identifications.
Apply kummer-limit-iso-detection for injectivity on classes and kummer-limit-class-lift for surjectivity; do not commute isomorphism classes with limits without these leaves.
Apply the exact finite fppf Kummer comparison at each exponent and retain its transition maps. The result is an identification with a chosen origin, not a loss of the automorphism groupoid.
acceptance: Changing neutralization translates the Kummer classes; no canonical origin is asserted.
The compatible roots-of2 torsor overQ is retained despite having no fppf local trivialization; H1_fppf(k,G) is not substituted for H1_fpqc(k,G).

nodes.title: The graded root Picard stack
nodes.statement: Pic_X^√R(S) is the groupoid of (L,K_R,ι), where L is a line bundle on X×S, K_R a line bundle on R×S and ι:K_R²≅L|_{R×S}. Its degree-d component imposes degree d on every geometric fibre; d ranges over all integers. Tensor product and dual give the graded commutative Picard stack.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Import the ordinary line-bundle Picard stack and restriction to R.
Take the root-gerbe two-pullback for the restricted line bundle; do not require a section.
Tensor and dual root data with the imported coherent line-bundle isomorphisms.
acceptance: Pic^d is a torsor component, with no chosen degree-one point required.

nodes.title: Square-action presentation of the root Picard stack
nodes.statement: Let Pic_{X,R} classify (L,γ:L|_R≅O_R). Then Pic_X^√R≃[Pic_{X,R}/[2]Res_{R/k}G_m], where the acting group changes the rigidification through its square. The forgetful morphism to Pic_X is a Res_{R/k}μ₂-gerbe.

proofSteps: Trivialize K_R fppf-locally; ι supplies the rigidification γ.
Changing the root-line frame by u changes γ by u², giving the square-action quotient.
The kernel is Res μ₂; verify the relative automorphism group and local lift property.

hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Add the actual section of K_R to the root-Picard objects and require arrows to preserve it.
The quotient description is the associated vector bundle with weight-one action on Res A¹ and square action on the rigidification.
acceptance: Requiring α_R≠0 or adding a global section changes this moduli problem.

nodes.title: Hat and effective root symmetric powers
nodes.statement: For d≥0 let hatX_d^√R classify (L,K_R,ι,a,α_R) of degree d with a∈Γ(X×S,L) and ι(α_R²)=a|_{R×S}. Define X_d^√R as the open where a is nonzero on every geometric fibre, and U_d^√R as the inverse image of Sym^d(X−R). Hat spaces admit zero global sections and nonreduced bases.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Impose the equality between the squared root section and the restriction of a.
Use the ordinary curve supplier to show fibrewise-nonzero sections define relative effective divisors of degree d.
Take the inverse image of divisors supported away from R.
acceptance: Nonzero means fibrewise nonzero, not merely a nonzero element of the total section group.

nodes.title: Evaluation description of root symmetric powers
nodes.statement: The root symmetric-power stack is the two-pullback of the ordinary evaluation map to [Res_R A¹/Res_R G_m] along its square-power map. Over a splitting field the latter is a product of copies of [A¹/G_m], one for each geometric point of R.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Evaluate the universal line bundle with section along R.
Identify the square-root fibre data with K_R,α_R,ι by the root two-pullback.
Descent through the finite étale splitting of R identifies the Weil restriction and product description.
acceptance: ρ is the number of geometric branch points after base change, not the number of closed points over k.

nodes.title: Incidence divisors meet transversely
nodes.statement: After splitting R, in Sym^d X each incidence divisor D_x of effective divisors containing x is smooth, and intersections for a subset I of distinct branch points identify with Sym^{d−|I|}X when d≥|I|, with codimension |I|; the intersection is empty when d<|I|.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Use addition of the fixed reduced divisor Σ_{x∈I}x to identify the intersection.
The ordinary symmetric-power supplier gives smoothness and dimension d−|I|.
Use the dimension calculation to obtain normal-crossing transversality.
acceptance: Repeated roots of the moving divisor do not replace distinct branch points in I.

nodes.title: The evaluation smoothness criterion
nodes.statement: For a smooth Z over the algebraically closed base, a map Z→[A^r/G_m^r] given by r line bundles with sections is smooth exactly when their zero divisors are smooth and meet transversely, including the empty strata.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Trivialize the line bundles and pull back the standard torus atlas.
Translate smoothness to the differential rank of the section coordinates on every vanishing stratum.
Smooth divisors and independent conormals supply that rank; conversely smoothness pulls back the coordinate normal-crossing strata.
acceptance: A zero section on all of Z fails the smooth divisor condition.

nodes.title: Smoothness of root symmetric powers
nodes.statement: The effective root symmetric power X_d^√R is smooth over k of dimension d and is DM. Its evaluation map to [Res_R A¹/Res_R G_m] is smooth.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Use the incidence calculation to show ordinary evaluation is smooth.
Pull that map back along the square-power classifying map to obtain root evaluation smoothness.
The root chart and invertibility of two give the smooth DM stack and its dimension.
acceptance: This is not a claim that the whole hat section space is smooth in arbitrary degree.

nodes.title: Addition of root divisors
nodes.statement: For d,e≥0 tensor L and K_R and multiply both sections to define hatadd_{d,e}:hatX_d^√R×hatX_e^√R→hatX_{d+e}^√R. Restriction gives addition on the effective opens; the same construction gives effective-divisor translation of the hat space.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Use tensor products of the two root isomorphisms.
The product section satisfies the restriction equation because tensor and restriction commute.
A product of fibrewise-nonzero sections on an integral smooth curve is fibrewise nonzero.
acceptance: The empty degree-zero divisor is the addition unit; root sections are multiplied, not added.

nodes.title: Properness and tame finite relative fibres
nodes.statement: The ordered map p_d is proper and quasi-finite in the nonrepresentable stack sense; the generic distinct-point locus is an S_d-cover. Its finite relative stabilizers are tame μ₂-products. No representably finite morphism is asserted at branch collisions.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: On coarse spaces use proper finite ordinary symmetric-power addition from the curve supplier.
The root stacks are proper over their coarse spaces and have finite tame inertia; apply the supplier’s properness comparison.
Compute collision stabilizers by the multiplication maps μ₂^m→μ₂; their kernels account for nonrepresentability.
acceptance: The two-equal-branch-point example detects misuse of a representable finite-map theorem.

nodes.title: Root Abel–Jacobi maps
nodes.statement: Define hatAJ_d:hatX_d^√R→Pic_X^√R,d by forgetting a and α_R, and the refined map retaining α_R to Pic_X^{√R;√R,d}. Restrict the first map to AJ_d:X_d^√R→Pic_X^√R,d. Addition commutes with the product AJ_d×AJ_e and Picard tensor multiplication.

proofSteps: Define both functors by explicit forgetful operations on objects and arrows.
Their composition forgets exactly the root section.
Compare tensoring and forgetting on data to obtain the product square with specified 2-isomorphism.
acceptance: The refined target retains α_R; the ordinary target does not.

Take the fibre product of multiplicative groups along reduction and the square homomorphism.

nodes.title: The adelic root Picard groupoid
nodes.statement: There is an equivalence Pic_X^√R(k)≃F×\A_F×/O_{√R}× as a double-action groupoid. The right action uses the actual noninjective homomorphism to idele units. Degree and all stabilizers are retained. At x∉R, π_x⁻¹ represents O_X(x)^♮.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Choose a generic trivialization of L and compatible local trivializations; the root-line frame along R yields the residue-square data.
Changing the generic and integral frames produces the left F× and right root-unit actions.
Reverse by gluing line bundles and root data, and identify automorphisms; use the divisor/idele dictionary with the π⁻¹ sign.
acceptance: For R=∅ recover the Picard groupoid, not just the class group; root-unit kernel elements remain stabilizers.

nodes.title: Rank-one local systems on the root curve
nodes.statement: Rank-one Q̄ℓ-local systems L on X_1^√R correspond to rank-one tame local systems on U=X−R whose geometric inertia characters have order dividing two. Their global monodromy can have arbitrary order; in particular an unramified character of order three is allowed.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Use local root charts to identify tame inertia with the residual μ₂ action.
A tame character factors through this action exactly when its local inertia square is one.
Glue using full faithful étale-local-system restriction and descent; the fundamental-group comparison for root stacks is the precise stack extension recorded in gap ST-LISSE.
acceptance: The quadratic cover supplies a special input, not the general definition.

nodes.title: Symmetric tensor local systems
nodes.statement: For L as above and d≥0 define K_d=(p_{d,!}L^{⊠d})^{S_d} with no shift, and L_d=H⁰(K_d). The collision and middle-extension lemmas prove K_d≅L_d, with L_d lisse rank one and L_d[d] perverse. The invariant projector is d!⁻¹Σσ over Q̄ℓ, including when ℓ divides d!.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Take the external tensor product with its genuine symmetry maps.
Apply the source-qualified tame stack proper pushforward, then the rational invariant projector.
Use the collision kernel and middle-extension lemmas below to prove this is lisse and concentrated in degree zero; the construction itself is the unshifted invariant complex.
acceptance: L_0=Q̄ℓ and L_1=L; the shift does not belong in the degree-zero local-system definition.

nodes.title: Collision kernels act trivially on the tensor line
nodes.statement: At a geometric divisor Σm_x x, the relative inertia of the ordered map over a branch point x is ker(μ₂^{m_x}→μ₂). It acts trivially on L_x^{⊗m_x}, since the same rank-one character occurs in every factor.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Describe root tensor addition on the stabilizer groups as multiplication.
Evaluate the tensor character as the product of the same character on each factor.
On the kernel this is the character of one, and permutation acts trivially on the ungraded rank-one tensor fibre.
acceptance: If the factors had unrelated inertia characters, the same kernel-triviality assertion would fail.

nodes.title: The symmetric complex is a shifted middle extension
nodes.statement: The rational invariant object (p_{d,!}L^{⊠d}[d])^{S_d} is the perverse intermediate extension of the distinct-point local system. Its unshifted stalks have no higher relative cohomology because the relative fibres are finite tame groupoids with rational coefficients.

nodes.title: Vanishing outside degree one for a nontrivial input
nodes.statement: If L is geometrically nontrivial on the proper root curve, H⁰(X_1^√R_kbar,L)=H²(X_1^√R_kbar,L)=0; its cohomology is concentrated in degree one.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Global invariant sections vanish for a geometrically nontrivial rank-one character.
The corresponding dual character is geometrically nontrivial, so smooth-DM Poincaré duality kills H².
Use the curve cohomological-dimension bound through the tame coarse-space comparison; its stack extension is recorded in ST-OPS.
acceptance: The constant sheaf is excluded: on P¹ it has nonzero H⁰ and H².

nodes.title: Graded symmetric invariants are exterior powers
nodes.statement: For a vector space V concentrated in cohomological degree one, the S_d-invariants of its d-fold graded tensor power are ∧^dV in degree d. The permutation action includes the Koszul sign, so this is the exterior rather than the ordinary symmetric power.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: A transposition acts by minus the ordinary flip on degree-one factors.
Thus the invariant projector is the antisymmetrizer; use the native exterior-power universal property over Q̄ℓ.
The total degree of d degree-one factors is d. The required comparison to the native exterior-power type is an explicit algebra API obligation, not a new exterior-algebra definition.
acceptance: For dim V=1 and d=2 the invariant space is zero; the ordinary symmetric square would be nonzero.

nodes.title: Exterior-power cohomology
nodes.statement: For geometrically nontrivial L, H^i(X_d^√R_kbar,L_d)=0 for i≠d, and H^d≅∧^dH¹(X_1^√R_kbar,L), naturally and Frobenius-equivariantly. This includes d=0; exterior powers vanish for d above dim H¹.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Apply the stack Künneth theorem and proper-pushforward cohomology comparison to the ordered product.
The rational invariant projector commutes with cohomology.
Identify the resulting graded invariants by the Koszul lemma.
acceptance: At d=0 the result is H⁰=Q̄ℓ; it does not contradict input H⁰ vanishing.

nodes.title: High-degree section evaluation is surjective
nodes.statement: If d≥ρ+max(2g−1,1), then for a degree-d line bundle L, H¹(X,L(−R))=0. In families, π_*L and π_*L(−R) are vector bundles of ranks d−g+1 and d−ρ−g+1, commute with base change, and π_*L→π_*(L|_R) is surjective.

proofSteps: Use Serre duality and the negative degree of ω_X⊗L⁻¹(R) to obtain H¹ vanishing.
Use the coherent base-change theorem for the smooth proper family to obtain locally free pushforwards and the evaluation exact sequence.

nodes.title: The Abel–Jacobi affine fibre chart

For ρ>0 and the degree bound, a splitting of evaluation identifies M≃A^n minus {0}, n=d−g+1. Scaling K_R by λ and L by λ² gives weights two on n−ρ coordinates and one on ρ coordinates.

ρ>0 and d≥ρ+max(2g−1,1).

nodes.title: Nontrivial intermediate weighted covers ramify
nodes.statement: A proper subgroup Γ⊊μ₂^a gives an intermediate cover of the weighted quotient that is ramified along at least one coordinate divisor x_i=0 in a chart where a weight-one coordinate y_ρ is nonzero. Hence such an intermediate cover cannot be finite étale.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: Choose a nontrivial character of μ₂^a/Γ, represented by a nonempty coordinate subset I.
On y_ρ≠0 its invariant root is the monomial ∏_{i∈I}x_i with square ∏_{i∈I}z_i.
This quadratic subcover ramifies along each z_i=0 for i∈I since two is invertible.
acceptance: The nonempty subset I and the weight-one affine chart are both required.

nodes.title: Simple connectivity of the weighted quotient
nodes.statement: The weighted quotient [A^n minus {0}/G_m] with weights (2^{n−ρ},1^ρ), ρ≥1 and n≥ρ+1, has no nontrivial connected finite étale cover. Thus every rank-one lisse Q̄ℓ-local system on it is geometrically constant.

proofSteps: Pull a connected finite étale cover back to P^{n−1}; the supplier’s projective-space simple connectivity makes that pullback trivial.

nodes.title: Local Hilbert 90 with root normalization
nodes.statement: As étale sheaves, ker Nm^√R is the image of u↦u/(σu), and ker(1−σ)=G_m,X inside ν_*G_m,X′. At ramification a root-normalized norm-one u has residue one, so w=1+u is locally a unit and u=w/(σw).
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: On the split locus use the explicit norm-one pair (u,u⁻¹).
At a branch point use σu=u⁻¹ and u|_{R′}=1; then 1+u is invertible because two is.
Invariant units descend through the finite-flat cover, giving the left kernel.
acceptance: Ordinary norm-one residue −1 is excluded by the root normalization; 1+u would fail there.

nodes.statement: Let K=ker Nm^√R. Interpret the exact sheaf complex as the two short exact sequences G_m→ν_*G_m→K and K→ν_*G_m→G_m^√R, and apply their derived cohomology and torsor descent. nodes.statement: For the geometrically connected double cover, ν_*Q̄ℓ decomposes into the ± eigensheaves of σ; its anti-invariant restriction to U is rank one, geometrically nontrivial and has inertia −1 exactly at R. nodes.statement: The Frobenius trace of L^Pic is a multiplicative Q̄ℓ×-valued function on isomorphism classes of Pic_X^√R(k), normalized to one at the tensor unit. Via the adelic equivalence it defines an idele character. For general input L its range is not restricted to {±1}.

nodes.title: Affine root-chart coaction
nodes.statement: Put B=A[t]/(tⁿ−f), using native AdjoinRoot, and H=A[Multiplicative(ZMod n)], using the native Hopf group algebra. Write e_i for its character basis element indexed by i modulo n. Define the unique A-algebra map δ:B→H⊗_A B with δ(t)=e_1⊗t. Constants map to 1⊗a. This is a universal coordinate map, not an action of the geometric-point set.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, f∈A and n≥1. No reducedness, nonzerodivisor or invertibility-of-n hypothesis is imposed.
proofSteps: In the native group algebra e_1ⁿ=e_0=1 because the character index is modulo n. Hence (e_1⊗t)ⁿ=1⊗f and the quotient polynomial evaluates to zero.
Apply the native AdjoinRoot algebra lift with this root and the coefficient map to H⊗_A B. The algebra-map law fixes constants.
Native quotient algebra-hom extensionality proves uniqueness. Counit and coassociativity are proved in separate nodes, not assumed fields.

nodes.title: Invariants of an affine root chart
nodes.statement: For every b∈B=A[t]/(tⁿ−f), δ(b)=1⊗b if and only if b=algebraMap(a) for some a∈A. Thus the scheme-theoretic invariant subalgebra is precisely the coefficient image, for all commutative A, f∈A and n≥1, including characteristic dividing n.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, f∈A and n≥1. No reducedness, nonzerodivisor or invertibility-of-n hypothesis is imposed.
proofSteps: Separate the subsingleton coefficient-ring case: its unital algebra B and tensor algebra are subsingleton, so both assertions hold with a=0. This avoids invoking the polynomial degree theorem without its nontriviality hypothesis.

For nontrivial A, Xⁿ−f is monic and has nat-degree n. Import the native monic AdjoinRoot power basis and reindex along that equality to write b uniquely as ∑_{0≤i<n} a_i t^i. The generic quotient basis is already library mathematics.

Use the weight lemma and the tensor-product basis of the native group-algebra basis and root power basis. In δ(b), a_i occurs at (i mod n,i); in 1⊗b it occurs at (0,i). For 0<i<n these index pairs differ, forcing a_i=0. This remains valid with torsion or nilpotents; it never divides by n or averages over field-valued points.
Only a_0 remains, giving b=algebraMap(a_0). Conversely the A-algebra-map law and tensor scalar relation give δ(algebraMap(a))=1⊗algebraMap(a).

Apply the separate native diagonal/zero-row coefficient criterion to the existing monic power-basis expansion, and use the coefficient algebra map for the reverse direction. The exact-pin native proof retains the separate zero-ring branch.
acceptance: At n=1 every element is a coefficient. At f=0 the nilpotent root powers remain independent. In characteristic p, field-point invariance is strictly weaker than δ-invariance.

The parentheses agree with tensorPower; these are canonical coordinates for that recursion, not a new tensor product.
hypotheses: Scheme X arbitrary; n a natural number, including zero.
proofSteps: Start with the identity at zero.
At the successor compose native tensorProductCongrLeft(c_n) with tensorTrivialRightIso(O). Their actual domains match the recursive tensor power.
For the section-unit API use the existing bilinear tensor-section/unit contract JAC-A; no generic section tensor map is constructed here.
acceptance: The exponent-one comparison is the native right-unit map, not an arbitrarily chosen scalar multiple.

nodes.title: The unit coefficient of a root identification
nodes.statement: For an actual n-th root object a=(M,t,φ) of (L,s), n≥1, and specified trivializations e:M≅O and l:L≅O, form α=c_n⁻¹ followed by (e⁻¹)ⁿ, φ and l, an automorphism of O. Let u be the coefficient of α(1). Then u is a unit in Γ(X,O_X); for every v∈Γ(X,Mⁿ), the coefficient of lφ(v) equals u times the coefficient of c_n eⁿ(v).
hypotheses: Scheme X arbitrary; n≥1; actual native invertible-sheaf isomorphisms φ,e,l.
proofSteps: Construct α from the stated isomorphisms, so it has an actual inverse.

Use pinned freeHomEquiv/unitHomEquiv: maps from the free one-generator sheaf are determined by the image of its unit section. On each open, module linearity makes α multiplication by its unit-section coefficient; naturality makes those coefficients restrictions of the global coefficient.
Apply the inverse map to obtain u v=1=v u in global functions. This proves IsUnit(u), rather than postulating it.
Apply the scalar evaluation formula to c_n eⁿ(v) and use the inverse/cancellation identities.
acceptance: Multiplication by 2 on O over Spec(Z/4) is not an allowed root identification. Nilpotents in the base do not invalidate multiplication by a unit.

nodes.statement: With the native root object and chosen trivializations above, the computed coefficient u is a unit and u zⁿ=f, where z is the coefficient of the root section under e and f is the coefficient of s under l. The coefficient u is part of the comparison; no choice of an n-th root of u is assumed.
hypotheses: Scheme X arbitrary; n≥1; root object and two specified native trivializations.
proofSteps: Use root-identification-unit to evaluate φ on the actual section tⁿ and establish that u is a unit.
Use section-power-in-trivialization to identify the coordinate of tⁿ with zⁿ.

Transport the defining root equation φ(tⁿ)=s by l; this gives u zⁿ=f. The example quantifies over a bundled unit and asserts equality to the computed coefficient, not just a renamed defining equation.
acceptance: Over Spec(Z/4), n=2, u=3 and z=2 give f=0 with z nonzero; zero sections and nilpotent roots must remain. Over Q the root object u=2,z=1,f=2 exists without a rational square root of 2.

nodes.statement: For root objects a,b of the same (L,s,n), chosen trivializations e_a,e_b of their root lines and l of L, every actual root arrow h:a→b has a unit coefficient w. The section coordinates satisfy z_b=w z_a and the computed root-identification coefficients satisfy u_b wⁿ=u_a. Retain both equations and the unit condition, including when sections vanish.
hypotheses: Scheme X arbitrary; n≥1; h is a native invertible root arrow, not an arbitrary module map.
proofSteps: Conjugate the underlying line isomorphism by e_a and e_b. The native free-sheaf Hom equivalence and its actual inverse give its unit coefficient w.
The arrow section equation gives z_b=w z_a.
Evaluate the tensor-power transport on the native unit section; sectionPower.mapIso and section-power-in-trivialization identify its coefficient with wⁿ.
Conjugate the arrow power equation φ_b∘hⁿ=φ_a by the chosen trivializations to obtain u_b wⁿ=u_a.
acceptance: For a=b with zero section and u_a=u_b, the power condition still forces wⁿ=1; forgetting it incorrectly makes every unit an automorphism. Composition multiplies w coefficients.

proofSteps: Use the zero-degree identity transport and the native unit section.
At the successor use JAC-A’s natural bilinear section tensor map with the native tensor congruences. Apply the induction hypothesis to the first factor and e to the second.

nodes.title: Fpqc descent of finite root data
nodes.statement: For every positive n and line bundle with section (L,s), the finite root-object pseudofunctor is a stack for the pinned fpqc topology, including on scheme test objects over a stack base. Thus its fppf restriction and its fpqc construction give the same root objects and arrows on every test scheme; the stronger descent assertion is a theorem, not an automatic change of topology.
hypotheses: Any fpqc scheme cover; a fixed (L,s) and positive n.
Tensor and unit pullback comparisons are the explicit JAC-A contract.
proofSteps: Apply the imported QCoh descent equivalence to the root line; rank-one finite-local-free detection makes the descended module invertible.
Regard a section as a module map O→M. Fullness descends that map, and the unit comparison identifies its domain.
Tensor/pullback comparisons identify the power of the descended line with the descent of the local powers. Descend the power isomorphisms and their inverses using full faithfulness.
The displayed section equation holds after the covering pullbacks; faithfulness makes it hold globally.
Apply the same full faithfulness to isomorphisms of root data and check their section and power equations; this proves effective object descent and sheaf descent for arrows.
acceptance: No reducedness, Noetherian or invertibility-of-the-exponent hypothesis is introduced.

Extend a factorial root system to level n by taking its finite transition from a factorial multiple. For two choices use a larger factorial and the supplied transition isomorphisms to compare them.

nodes.title: The fpqc Kummer torsor tower
nodes.statement: Over a field k let G=lim_(n|m) μ_n in the fpqc topology, with transition μ_(nm)→μ_n given by the mth power. The groupoid of fpqc G-torsors is equivalent to the two-limit of the groupoids of finite μ_n-torsors, with specified quotient comparisons and their cocycles. No finite-presentation or etale-local-triviality assertion for G is made.
hypotheses: A field k of arbitrary characteristic.
Infinite torsors are fpqc; finite μ_n torsors may be computed fppf.
proofSteps: The compatible trivial finite torsors give an actual k-object of the two-limit; nonemptiness is supplied rather than assumed away.
Apply the imported affine fpqc limit-gerbe theorem. Its automorphism sheaf at that object is exactly G, because an automorphism is a compatible sequence of finite translations.
Use the imported neutralization equivalence with that fixed object. Evaluation at each level is extension of torsors through G→μ_n.
On an affine cover the inverse is the compatible affine limit of finite torsors; the exact affine faithful-flat limit contract remains TOWER-AFF.
acceptance: No reducedness, Noetherian or invertibility-of-the-exponent hypothesis is introduced.

nodes.title: Finite stages detect Kummer tower isomorphisms
nodes.statement: Two compatible finite μ_n-torsor towers over a field k are isomorphic if their n-th torsors are isomorphic for every positive n. Individual finite-stage isomorphisms need not be chosen compatibly in advance.
hypotheses: Compatible finite μ_n-torsor towers over a field; equality of their finite-stage isomorphism classes.
proofSteps: For each n take the set of equivariant k-isomorphisms between the two nth torsors. It is nonempty by the premise.
Once one isomorphism is fixed, this set is a torsor for μ_n(k); the pinned roots-of-unity equivalence and finite instance make it finite, even when μ_n is not etale.
The coherent tower quotient maps induce the restriction maps on these finite sets. Positive divisibility gives a cofiltered index category.
Apply the existing nonempty finite-system theorem to obtain a compatible sequence of isomorphisms. The groupoid limit comparison turns it into the required arrow.

nodes.title: The infinite affine fpqc root quotient
nodes.statement: For B_n=A[T]/(T^n−f) with the displayed divisibility maps, put B_infinity=colim_n B_n and G=lim_n μ_n, with its diagonalizable grading action. The infinite root stack of (O_A,f) is [Spec B_infinity/G] as an fpqc quotient stack. Its morphism groupoids and finite projections agree with the two-limit of the finite roots. This is not asserted to be an algebraic stack of finite presentation.
hypotheses: Any commutative ring A and f∈A.
Infinite quotient and torsors use the fpqc topology; TOWER-AFF is an explicit supplier obligation.
proofSteps: Use the existing actual factorial algebra C_f and its checked finite-coordinate API. The positive-divisibility comparison identifies it with C_div by mutually inverse native algebra maps, carrying every positive root v_n to u_i^(d_i/n) at any factorial multiple. The diagonalizable grading, Spec-limit transport and coherent fpqc torsor/root-groupoid contracts are separate remaining steps; no geometric conclusion follows merely from this algebra comparison.
For every compatible root system over T, form the finite frame torsors respecting its power identifications. Their maps are the finite μ transitions and are affine faithfully flat.
The TOWER-AFF contract makes their inverse limit an affine fpqc G-torsor; its universal frames give an equivariant map to Spec B_infinity.
Conversely an equivariant G-torsor map supplies the finite root data by finite quotient and the root-coordinate functions.
Compare the two constructions on objects and torsor arrows, with their finite-stage and base-change coherence.

The actual coherent-unit point families now have constructed automorphisms on C_f with root/coefficient, identity/composition and inverse formulas. This point interface is not the universal diagonalizable Hopf action and does not discharge the Spec-limit, fpqc torsor or quotient-groupoid obligations.

The actual coherent scalar point/scaling interface now commutes with every coefficient ring homomorphism, including the actual inverse maps. Use the specified φ-semilinear chart map and its root/coefficient functor laws; this is still an algebraic point-natural action, not the universal diagonalizable Hopf coaction or a Spec/fpqc quotient comparison.

The actual factorial Hopf/coaction interface now supplies counitality, coassociativity, antipode identities, represented algebra-valued points and specialization to inherited scaling. Use these checked rank-one algebra maps as input, then separately identify the canonical diagonalizable coordinate Hopf algebra, its point convolution group and the transported positive-index action. The existing Spec-limit, coherent frame torsor and fpqc quotient-groupoid constructions are still required; no geometric conclusion is inferred from these algebra formulas.

Before the separate geometric quotient construction, use the actual coaction, counit and antipode coefficient-naturality identities. They provide compatible ring maps on coefficients and all factorial roots; they do not supply the remaining fpqc frame-torsor or quotient-stack equivalence.

Use the actual convolution point/coherent-root multiplicative equivalence and its antipode inverse and test-algebra naturality. Import the existing Tau Ceti convolution-group instance, whose inverse is p∘S, rather than constructing another generic point group. The A[Q/Z] coordinate Hopf comparison, universe transports, root-object reindexing, affine Spec limits, fpqc frame torsors and geometric quotient equivalence remain distinct obligations.

Use the actual convolution action on chart algebra-valued points, its native action laws, inverse cancellation, naturality and universal tensor recovery. Fixed zero-root points expressly prevent inferring a free action or torsor from these formulas. The A[Q/Z] coordinate comparison, universe/index transports, coherent root-object groupoids, affine Spec limits, fpqc frame torsors and quotient-groupoid equivalence remain independent obligations.

Use the actual finite unity-root equivalence E_n:B_n(1)≃A[Z/n], whose root and inverse-basis formulas intertwine the existing coaction with native comultiplication, identify counit/root antipode, and carry divisibility transitions to [k]↦[(N/n)k]. Then separately construct compatible Z/n→Q/Z embeddings and identify the colimit as A[Q/Z], including all Hopf maps. No infinite coordinate or geometric quotient conclusion follows from the finite equivalences alone.

Use the planned normalized finite character embeddings and actual unity-root colimit equivalence with A[Q/Z], together with its separate comultiplication, counit, antipode and coefficient squares. These provide the canonical fixed-universe coordinate Hopf input. Their new prototypes are uncompiled and every declaration remains unchecked. Still construct index/universe transports, coherent root-object reindexing, affine Spec limits and fpqc frame torsors before the geometric quotient equivalence; no such geometric obligation is discharged by this coordinate plan.

Use the actual arbitrary-section rational coaction η_f=(E_A⊗id)ρ_f, its native counit/coassociativity laws and unity compatibility to pin the Q/Z diagonalizable grading. Native tensor coordinate equivalence reflects universal coinvariance, not invariance under field-valued points. Coefficient naturality, higher-universe/full-index transport and geometric fpqc frame descent remain separate obligations.

Use the native heterobasic rational-character coefficient map Q_(φ,f), its composition law, the actual η coefficient square and one-way coinvariance preservation. These remain conditional algebraic inputs; higher universes, full positive-index/groupoid transport, Spec limits and fpqc frame/quotient comparisons remain independent obligations. Coefficient naturality does not assert injectivity or reflection for nonflat maps.

nodes.title: A degree bound for roots of two
nodes.statement: If K/Q is a finite field extension and x∈K satisfies x^n=2 for positive n, then n≤[K:Q]. In particular no finite extension of Q contains compatible nth roots of2 for every positive n.
hypotheses: K is a field with a Q-algebra structure and finite dimension over Q; n>0.
proofSteps: The monic integer polynomial X^n−2 satisfies Eisenstein at (2): nonleading coefficients are divisible by2 and its constant coefficient is not divisible by4.
Gauss comparison makes X^n−2 irreducible over Q.
Its root equation and monicity identify it with minpoly_Q(x).
The native degree bound gives n≤finrank_Q K. Choose n larger than that dimension to exclude roots at all levels.
acceptance: For K=Q, only the n=1 case can have a root of2. A quadratic field may contain a square root but cannot contain a cube root of2. All positive n, including composite n, are covered by Eisenstein.

nodes.title: An infinite Kummer torsor requiring fpqc descent
nodes.statement: Over Q, the compatible finite torsors P_n=Spec Q[T]/(T^n−2) define an fpqc G=lim_n μ_n torsor P_infinity. It has no section after any nonempty fppf Q-cover. Each individual P_n is fppf-locally trivial, so replacing all infinite torsors by fppf-locally trivial G-torsors loses this point of the infinite classifying gerbe.
hypotheses: Base field Q; all positive root exponents.
The finite-type chart and closed-point residue comparison are the exact SF.1 contract.
proofSteps: The element2 is a unit; each finite root chart is a μ_n torsor. The transition equations provide a coherent tower.
The fpqc torsor-limit comparison constructs P_infinity; the finite-free transition calculation also exhibits its affine fpqc cover.
Suppose it has a section on a nonempty fppf Q-scheme. Choose a nonempty affine finite-type open chart and a closed point. Its residue field is finite over Q by the pinned Zariski lemma.
Specialize the section to that field. It would contain an nth root of2 for every n, contradicting the degree-bound leaf.
acceptance: Every finite P_n is an fppf torsor, while their actual fpqc limit admits no nonempty fppf trivializing cover. The contradiction retains the finite residue-field degree, rather than choosing a field of unbounded degree.

nodes.title: Affine action comparison
nodes.statement: Let B=A[x]/(xⁿ−f) be native AdjoinRoot and H=A[Multiplicative(ZMod n)] the native Hopf group algebra, with character basis e_i. Define the A-algebra map Θ:B⊗_A B→H⊗_A B by the tensor universal property applied to δ:B→H⊗B and c↦1⊗c. Thus the right B-factor is unchanged; this is the coordinate map of the action comparison, not a freely chosen linear map.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.
proofSteps: Use the existing affine coaction and the native right-factor algebra inclusion. Their images commute because the target algebra is commutative.
Apply the native tensor-algebra lift, with these two specified maps. Its algebra-map laws fix coefficients and define a unique comparison; no torsor predicate or geometric-point set is introduced.

nodes.title: Source coefficient equivalence
nodes.statement: For B=A[x]/(xⁿ−f), H=A[Multiplicative(ZMod n)] and any commutative ring A with positive n, construct the specified A-linear equivalence B⊗_A B ≃ ((Fin n×Fin n)→A) extracting the unique coefficients in the ordered vectors x^i⊗x^j. hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.
proofSteps: Define the native synthesis linear map by the finite linear combination in the statement. Linearity follows from addition and scalar multiplication distributing over a finite sum.
The listed coordinate existence-and-uniqueness lemma proves synthesis bijective: uniqueness gives injectivity and existence gives surjectivity.

Apply LinearEquiv.ofBijective to synthesis and take its inverse. The inverse evaluation is the exact sum, the forward evaluation of a synthesized family follows from the inverse law, and synthesis of a single coefficient gives the generator formula.

nodes.title: Weighted permutation formula
nodes.statement: For 0≤i,j<n, Θ(x^i⊗x^j)=f^⌊(i+j)/n⌋(e_i⊗x^((i+j) mod n)). The exponent is zero or one. The target index σ(i,j)=(i,(i+j) mod n) is a permutation: its inverse sends (i,k) to (i,k−i) when k≥i and to (i,n+k−i) when k<i.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.
proofSteps: Use the pure-tensor formula and the coaction weight law to obtain e_i⊗x^(i+j).
Use the actual quotient relation xⁿ=f and Euclidean division i+j=nq+r. Tensor balancing moves f^q to the coefficient.
Check the two displayed inverse indices are between zero and n−1, with sum wrapping exactly in the k<i branch. This proves bijectivity of σ without cancellation in A.
acceptance: The n=2 column (1,1) maps to f times target (1,0), explaining both branch and nonunit obstructions.

nodes.title: Kernel coefficient criterion
nodes.statement: For c:(Fin n×Fin n)→A, Θ(Σ c_(i,j)(x^i⊗x^j))=0 iff c_(i,j)=0 when i+j<n and f c_(i,j)=0 when i+j≥n.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.
proofSteps: Rewrite the source sum as the specified synthesis inverse. For a zero image, extract the target coefficient at σp and use the complete coefficient table.
The wrap/lower equivalence gives precisely the nonwrapping zero and wrapping f-annihilation conditions.
Conversely evaluate every target coefficient q using σ⁻¹q and apply the assumed equations. Injectivity of the native target coordinate equivalence gives the zero image.
acceptance: The coefficient 2 in wrapping coordinate (1,1) lies in the kernel for A=Z/4,f=2.

nodes.title: Image coefficient criterion
nodes.statement: For d:(Fin n×Fin n)→A, Σ d_(i,k)(e_i⊗x^k) belongs to the A-linear range of Θ iff d_(i,k)∈fA for every k<i. There is no restriction on coordinates with k≥i.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.
proofSteps: For a preimage z, use its actual source coordinates in the coefficient table. Every lower target coefficient is f times the source coefficient at σ⁻¹q.
Conversely choose a factor for each of the finitely many lower coefficients; use the coefficient itself elsewhere. Define the source family by transport along σ.
Synthesize that source family. Its image has exactly the target coefficients by the weighted table and the promoted target-extraction identity. Target coordinate injectivity proves equality.
The existing principal-ideal membership criterion identifies these f-multiple conditions with membership in fA.

nodes.title: Coordinate kernel equivalence
nodes.statement: Let W={(i,j)∈Fin n×Fin n:n≤i+j}. The native A-linear kernel of Θ is A-linearly equivalent to functions W→ann_A(f), where ann_A(f) is the kernel of multiplication by f on A. The forward map sends a kernel tensor to its W-coordinates in the source monic basis.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.
proofSteps: Take the specified wrapping kernel coordinate equivalence.
Apply its extraction formula and the existing source coefficient formula on every finite basis expansion. This proves the original existential statement with its specified forward map.
acceptance: At n=1 W is empty, so the kernel is zero for every f, including f=0.

hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.

nodes.title: Sharp injectivity criterion
nodes.statement: The A-algebra comparison Θ is injective iff n=1 or the map a↦fa on A is injective.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.
proofSteps: For n=1 every coefficient is nonwrapping, so the kernel criterion makes the kernel zero.
For n>1 the source position (1,n−1) is wrapping. Place a−b there; if fa=fb the kernel criterion kills its actual synthesized tensor. Injectivity and source coefficient extraction imply a=b.
Conversely apply the kernel criterion to the source coordinate family of z−w. Injectivity of multiplication by f kills every wrapping coefficient, and target equality gives z=w.
acceptance: For Z,n=2,f=2 the map is injective although f is not a unit.

nodes.statement: The comparison Θ is surjective iff n=1 or f is a unit in A.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.

The zero ring is included, and no inverse of n enters.

nodes.title: Weighted comparison determinant
nodes.statement: In the specified source and target pair-indexed bases, the comparison matrix has entry M_(r,c)=f^⌊(c₁+c₂)/n⌋ if r₁=c₁ and r₂=(c₁+c₂) mod n, and zero otherwise. With E=n(n−1)/2, det M=(−1)^((n−1)E) f^E. The same pair ordering is used for rows and columns; this is not an endomorphism determinant without chosen identifications.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, n≥1 and f∈A, unless the statement specifies a field or a unit. No reducedness, domain, flatness of coefficient change or invertibility-of-n assumption.
proofSteps: Consume matrix_reindex for the specified monomial support and inverse coefficient permutation. Apply the pinned determinant-permutation and diagonal determinant formulas.
Consume coefficientPermutation_sign and the native inverse-sign law. Cast the already computed integer-unit sign into A.
Consume weight_product for the exact column weights. Their count E is computed in natural numbers, not by dividing by2 in A. Combine sign and weight without cancellation.
acceptance: For n=2 the determinant is −f, including f=0 and nonreduced coefficient rings.

nodes.title: Specified wrapping kernel coordinates
nodes.statement: With W={(i,j):n≤i+j} and ann_A(f)=ker(f•id_A), construct the specified native A-linear equivalence ker_A Θ ≃ (W→ann_A(f)). Its forward map extracts C_s(z) on W. Its inverse applies C_s⁻¹ to the family equal to d_p on W and zero elsewhere.

hypotheses: A,B,C are arbitrary commutative rings in one fixed universe, with specified A-algebra structures on B and C; k:B→C is an arbitrary A-algebra homomorphism. No nontriviality, characteristic, invertible-order, reducedness, domain, finite-presentation or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

H_A is the existing actual factorial affine colimit C_A(1), h_i its distinguished roots of order (i+1)!, Δ the inherited unity coaction, ε its counit and S its antipode. The local bialgebra is the existing factorialBialgebra A; its Hopf structure is the existing factorialHopfAlgebra A. S_B is the existing subgroup factorialRootScalars B, P_B the existing factorialScalarPoints equivalence and E_B its existing evaluation inverse.

The native Mathlib convolution multiplication is used on WithConv of actual A-algebra homomorphisms, not pointwise multiplication of ring maps. The existing Tau Ceti group instance has the same multiplication and inverse p∘S. This comparison does not identify H_A with A[Q/Z], transport universes, reindex root-object groupoids or prove fpqc quotient descent.
proofSteps: Compare the unit values at every index using injectivity of unit values and subtype extensionality; use the root-coordinate convolution formula.
acceptance: The existing point equivalence P_B:AlgHom_A(H_A,B)≃S_B sends the underlying algebra homomorphism of p*q in the native convolution monoid to P_B(p)P_B(q) in the actual subgroup S_B of coherent unit families.

tests.name: convolutionPointsTests.degree_two

tests.name: convolutionPointsTests.roundtrip
tests.statement: For every actual native convolution point p, Q_B⁻¹(Q_B(p))=p.

tests.name: convolutionPointsTests.inverse
tests.statement: For every algebra point p, convolution of p∘S_A with p is the native convolution identity.

tests.name: convolutionPointsTests.zero_ring
tests.statement: For A=B=Z/1Z, the actual point comparison sends the native convolution identity to the unique coherent family1.

tests.name: convolutionPointsTests.counit_not_identity

tests.name: convolutionPointsTests.naturality

nodes.title: The universal finite cyclic root character
nodes.statement: Define χ_n:Multiplicative(ZMod n)→*B_n by χ_n([k])=t_n^val(k), where B_n=A[T]/(T^n−1).
hypotheses: A is an arbitrary commutative ring in one fixed universe; n is a positive natural number. If N occurs it is positive and n divides N. No nontriviality, reducedness, field, Noetherian, characteristic or invertibility-of-n hypothesis is imposed.

B_n is the inherited actual AffineRing (1:A) n = AdjoinRoot(X^n−C1); t_n is its root. The target is the inherited MuHopf A n = MonoidAlgebra A (Multiplicative (ZMod n)); e_[k]=single(ofAdd k) 1. This is the unity-parameter coordinate algebra of μ_n, not the arbitrary-f chart algebra.

The finite comparison supplies one input to identifying the factorial unity-root Hopf algebra with A[Q/Z]. That infinite Hopf identification, rational-circle maps, arbitrary-universe adapters, affine Spec limits, coherent frame torsors and fpqc quotient comparison remain open.
proofSteps: The existing root-power reduction with f=1 makes t_n^k periodic modulo n. Use val(k+l)=(val(k)+val(l)) mod n to prove multiplicativity; zero maps to one.
acceptance: Define χ_n:Multiplicative(ZMod n)→*B_n by χ_n([k])=t_n^val(k), where B_n=A[T]/(T^n−1).

stageAssignments.title: Normalized symplectic Frobenius and central square classes
Quaternionic tests beyond the main hypotheses

contract.name: Functional equation and ε-factors with torsion coefficients
contract.statement: L(X, ρ, t) = ε(ρ, t) L(X, ρ^∨, 1/(qt)) with ε(ρ, t) = αt^m (α ∈ ℓ^×, m ∈ Z), and ε(ρ) = Π_x ε_x(ρ, ψ, μ) for an additive character ψ of the adeles and a factorized measure (Deligne, 'Les constantes des équations fonctionnelles', Thm. 7.11, (7.9.1)); ε_x = ε_{0,x}·det(−F_x q^{deg(x)/2} | V^{I_x}) (7.6.3), and ε_{0,x}(ρ ⊗ χ) = ε_{0,x}(χ)^{dim ρ} for unramified ρ of trivial determinant ((5.5.3)).

contract.name: The normalized Frobenius is special orthogonal
contract.statement: Let ρ : π_1(X) → Sp_{2r}(ℓ) with √q ∈ ℓ fixed and H^0 = H^2 = 0 geometrically. Then H^1(X_{k̄}, ρ) has dimension 2(dim ρ)(g − 1), a symmetric pairing with ⟨Fx, Fy⟩ = q⟨x, y⟩, and F̄ = q^{−1/2}F ∈ SO(H^1): ε(ρ, t) = (−√q t)^{dim H^1} det F̄ and ε(ρ, 1/√q) = 1 for unramified ρ of trivial determinant.
contract.note: The printed intermediate formula for ε is off by q^{dim H^1}; see sourceIssues E5.

contract.name: The square classes L(X, ρ) and L^*(X, ρ)
contract.statement: L(X, ρ) is the image of L(X, ρ, 1/√q) in ℓ^×/2 when nonzero; in general L^*(X, ρ) = spinor norm(F̄) = (h!·det⟨v_i, v_j⟩)^{−1}(d^h/dt^h)L(X, ρ, t)|_{t=1/√q} ∈ ℓ^×/2, where h (even) is the order of vanishing, the dimension of the generalized fixed space of F on H^1(X_{k̄}, ρ), with basis v_1, …, v_h. For GSp-valued ρ^{(g)} with cyclotomic multiplier and ρ = ρ^{(g)}(−1/2), L(X, ρ^{(g)}) is the square class of L(X, ρ^{(g)}, 1) = L(X, ρ, 1/√q).
contract.note: The second equality is Zassenhaus's formula (Appendix B.9.1) applied to the even-dimensional H^1 of square discriminant.

contract.name: Lemma 3.5.1 and §3.5: square discriminant of H^1
contract.statement: For a closed oriented surface Σ and ρ : π_1(Σ) → Sp_{2r}(ℓ), ℓ finite, the quadratic form on H^*(Σ, ρ) (the cup-product form on H^1, and the Poincaré pairing between H^0 and H^2) has square discriminant. Consequently, by lifting to the Witt vectors and to C, H^1(X_{k̄}, ρ) has square discriminant and L(X, ρ) does not depend on the choice of √q.
contract.note: Proof: the discriminant is a bordism invariant (a Lagrangian image and dim H^* ≡ 0 mod 4), giving MSO_2(BSp_{2r}(ℓ)) = H_2(Sp_{2r}(ℓ), Z) → ℓ^×/2, which vanishes because H_2 has odd order (sourceIssues E3).

contract.name: The trace map and c_et(X, ρ)
contract.statement: For A finite of order prime to p, the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence and the trace H^2(X_{k̄}, A(1)) ≅ A give trace_X : H^3_et(X, A(1)) ≅ H^1(Gal(k̄/k), A) ≅ A (via the Frobenius generator). For ρ : π_1(X) → Sp(ℓ), c_et(X, ρ) := trace_X(ρ^*c_et) ∈ ℓ^×/2 (A = ℓ^×/2 ≅ Z/2).

contract.name: Admissible and GSp-admissible pairs
contract.statement: (X, ρ), with X a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over k = F_q and ρ : π_1(X) → Sp_{2r}(ℓ), is admissible if (a1) ρ is geometrically surjective, (a2) q is prime to #Sp_{2r}(ℓ), (a3) q is a square in the prime field of ℓ. It is GSp-admissible (ρ : π_1(X) → GSp_{2r}(ℓ) with cyclotomic multiplier) if (a1)′ the geometric image contains Sp_{2r}(ℓ) and (a2)′ q is prime to #GSp_{2r}(ℓ). Admissible implies GSp-admissible for ρ^{(g)}.

contract.name: Theorem 3.1: the main theorem
contract.statement: Let (X, ρ) be admissible, #ℓ ≡ ±1 (mod 8) and q ≡ 1 (mod 8). Then L(X, ρ) = c_et(X, ρ) in ℓ^×/2 (with L = L^* when the central value vanishes).
contract.note: The proof in v1 does not cover r = 1, #ℓ = 9 (sourceIssues E4).

contract.name: Equivalence of the Sp and GSp formulations
contract.statement: For ρ = ρ^{(g)}(−1/2): L(X, ρ^{(g)}) = L(X, ρ) and c_et(X, ρ^{(g)}) = c_et(X, ρ), since the class on GSp(ℓ) pulls back along π_1(X) → Sp(ℓ) × Ẑ → GSp(ℓ) to c_et ⊗ 1 plus a term in H^2(Sp(ℓ), ℓ^×/2) ⊗ ℓ^×/2 = 0.

contract.name: Lemma 3.9.1: even valuation of central values of compatible systems
contract.statement: Let {σ_λ : π_1(X) → GSp_{2r}(o_{E,λ})} be a compatible system (traces of Frobenius powers in E, independent of λ ∤ p), with L(X, σ, t) ∈ E(t). If λ ∤ 2p and σ_λ has geometric image Zariski dense in Sp_{2r}, then the valuation at λ of L(X, σ) = L(X, σ, 1), if nonzero, is even.
contract.note: The spinor norm of an orthogonal map preserving a unimodular lattice has even valuation (O'Meara 92:5).

contract.name: Larsen's big-image theorem for compatible systems
contract.statement: For a compatible system {σ_λ} with Zariski-dense image, for a density-one set of λ the image of σ_λ in PSp_{2r}(E_λ) contains a conjugate of the image of Sp_{2r}(o_λ) (Larsen, Thm. 3.17).

contract.name: §3.10 (*): Theorem 3.1 determines L-values of compatible systems
contract.statement: Let {σ_λ} be a compatible system of GSp_{2r}-valued representations over X/F_q, q ≡ 1 (mod 8), with L(X, σ) ≠ 0, such that (a) the p-cyclotomic extension of E(√2) has degree > 4r² and (b) σ_λ has Zariski-dense image for a density-one set of λ. Then Theorem 3.1 applied to the reductions of σ determines the square class of L(X, σ) in E(√q)^×/2 up to multiplication by 2.
contract.note: Not used elsewhere in the paper.

contract.name: The defect δ(X, ρ) and Frobenius of k
contract.statement: δ(X, ρ) := L^*(X, ρ)/c_et(X, ρ) ∈ ℓ^×/2 (similarly for GSp-admissible ρ^{(g)}). For M/Q finite Galois unramified at p, Frob_k ∈ Gal(M/Q) is the conjugacy class of Frob(ϖ/p)^n for q = p^n.

contract.name: Step A: the defect is a Dirichlet character
contract.statement: For fixed r and ℓ there is a quadratic character χ_{r,ℓ} : Gal(Q̄/Q) → {±1}, unramified outside the primes dividing #Sp_{2r}(ℓ), such that δ(X, ρ) = χ_{r,ℓ}(Frob_k) (under {±1} ≅ ℓ^×/2) for every GSp-admissible (X, ρ) over k.
contract.note: The proof uses Lemma 5.1.1, which fails for r = 1, #ℓ = 9 (sourceIssues E4).

contract.name: Step B: χ_{r,ℓ} is unramified outside 2ℓ
contract.statement: For #ℓ ≡ ±1 (mod 8), the character χ_{r,ℓ} of Step A is unramified outside 2ℓ: for each odd prime m ≠ ℓ there is a Galois extension M* of Q unramified at m such that for every sufficiently large prime p split in M* there is a GSp-admissible (X, ρ) over F_{p^j}, j odd, with δ(X, ρ) = 1.

contract.name: Steps A and B imply Theorem 3.1
contract.statement: If χ_{r,ℓ} is unramified outside 2ℓ then χ_{r,ℓ}(Frob_p) = (Z/p) with Z ∈ ⟨−1, 2, ℓ_0⟩; writing Z = Z_0 or Z_0ℓ_0′ (ℓ_0′ = (−1)^{(ℓ_0−1)/2}ℓ_0) and using (ℓ_0′/p)^n = (q/ℓ_0) = 1 for admissible (X, ρ), δ(X, ρ) = (Z_0/p)^n, a character mod 8 of q = p^n, which is 1 when q ≡ 1 (mod 8).

contract.name: Hurwitz stacks 𝔐^G_g and 𝔐^{G*}_g
contract.statement: For G = Sp_{2r}(ℓ), N = #G: the Deligne–Mumford stack 𝔐^G_g over Z[1/N] of smooth projective genus-g curves Σ/S with a finite étale G-torsor f : Σ̃ → Σ whose geometric fibres Σ̃_s are irreducible; and its twisted form 𝔐^{G*}_g for G̃ = GSp_{2r}(ℓ) with an identification of the associated ℓ^×-cover with the cyclotomic one (fibres with #ℓ − 1 components). Over C a component is 𝒯/Γ̃_0 for Teichmüller space 𝒯 and the central extension Γ̃_0 of the stabilizer Γ_0 of a surjection π_1(Σ) → G by Z(G); 𝔐^G_g is a gerbe over Deligne–Mumford's stack of Teichmüller level structures. Admissible pairs give k-points of 𝔐^G_g, GSp-admissible pairs k-points of 𝔐^{G*}_g.

contract.name: Livingston–Dunfield–Thurston: mapping class group orbits on surjections
contract.statement: For a finite group G with H_2(G, Z) = 0 and g sufficiently large, the mapping class group of a closed genus-g surface Σ acts transitively on the set of conjugacy classes of surjections π_1(Σ) → G (Dunfield–Thurston, Thm. 6.25, after Livingston). In general the orbits are classified by the image of [Σ] in H_2(G, Z).
contract.note: The paper notes that Dunfield–Thurston's Theorem 6.25 is slightly misstated (the action is by the mapping class group modulo the group).

contract.name: Lemma 5.1.1: irreducibility in large genus
contract.statement: If H_2(Sp_{2r}(ℓ), Z) = 0, i.e. unless r = 1 and #ℓ = 9, there is g_0(r, ℓ) such that for g ≥ g_0 the Q̄-fibre of 𝔐^G_g is irreducible (and so is that of 𝔐^{G*}_g).
contract.note: Stated as corrected; the paper asserts it for all (r, ℓ) (sourceIssues E4).

contract.name: The universal classes 𝔜 and 𝔜′
contract.statement: On the universal curve π : 𝔘* → 𝔐^{G*} with its G̃-cover 𝔘* → BG̃: 𝔜 ∈ H^1_et(𝔐^{G*}, Z/2) is π_*(pullback of c_et) (trace shifting degree by 2), and 𝔜′ ∈ H^1(𝔐^{G*}, ℓ^×/2) classifies the spinor-norm torsor of the orthogonal local system 𝒪 = R^1π_*𝒮 (𝒮 the symplectic ℓ-local system, with pairing to ℓ(1)). For a GSp-admissible (X, ρ) over k, 𝔜 and 𝔜′ specialize to c_et(X, ρ) and L(X, ρ) in H^1(k, Z/2) = k^×/2.
contract.note: Uses étale cohomology of Artin stacks (Laszlo–Olsson).

contract.name: Lemma 5.2.1: 𝔜 = 𝔜′ on the geometric generic fibre
contract.statement: 𝔜 and 𝔜′ coincide on 𝔐^{G*}_{Q̄}.
contract.note: For a loop γ, 𝔜(γ) = trace_M(ρ^*c_et) on the mapping torus M and 𝔜′(γ) = spinor norm of the monodromy on H^1(fibre, ρ), equal by (1.5); here the coefficients are finite, where the paper proves (1.5) only in characteristic 0 (sourceIssues E25). The stack is handled through a smooth cover (Y × E)/Δ with E an approximation of BΔ (Totaro).

contract.name: Lemma 5.3.1: 𝔜 − 𝔜′ comes from Z[1/N]
contract.statement: For g ≥ g_0(r, ℓ), 𝔜 − 𝔜′ is the pullback to 𝔐^{G*} of a class in H^1(Z[1/N], Z/2), i.e. of a quadratic character unramified outside N.
contract.note: Uses irreducibility (Lemma 5.1.1), purity (injectivity of H^1(𝔐^{G*}) → H^1(𝔐^{G*}_Q)) and W-points of 𝔐^{G*} for each w ∤ N (Sp_{2r}(ℓ) is 2-generated).

contract.name: §5.4 Claim: odd-degree cyclic covers preserve δ
contract.statement: Let (X, ρ) be GSp-admissible, m odd and prime to ℓ with ℓ of odd order t modulo m, and f : X̃ → X a Z/m-Galois cover by a geometrically irreducible smooth proper curve. Then (X̃, f^*ρ) is GSp-admissible and δ(X, ρ) = δ(X̃, f^*ρ).
contract.note: c_et is preserved since f^* : H^3(X, Z/2) → H^3(X̃, Z/2) is an isomorphism; for L^* the Artin decomposition over the characters of Z/m, the functional equation and §5.4.1 show the extra factors are squares.

contract.name: §5.4.1: ε-factors of twists of symplectic systems
contract.statement: For ρ symplectic and unramified with det ρ = 1 and χ a character, ε(ρ ⊗ χ) = ε(χ)^{dim ρ} (an equality, not only of square classes); in particular ε(ρ ⊗ χ) is a square.

contract.name: §5.5 Claim: raising the genus
contract.statement: For each GSp-admissible (X, ρ) over k there is g_0′(X, ρ) such that for every g ≥ g_0′ there is a GSp-admissible (X′, ρ′) of genus g over k with δ(X′, ρ′) = δ(X, ρ).
contract.note: X′ is a ramified Z/M-cover, M a product of primes m ≡ 3 (mod 4) with q and ℓ of odd order mod m and gcd of the (m−1)/2 equal to 1, built by class field theory and Riemann–Hurwitz.

contract.name: §6.1 Claim: totally real fields with prescribed unit reduction
contract.statement: For a finite field ℓ with #ℓ ≡ ±1 (mod 8) and an odd prime m ≠ char ℓ, there is a totally real field F with (i) [F:Q] ≥ 3, (ii) D_F prime to m, (iii) a prime λ_0 with o_F/λ_0 ≅ ℓ such that U_F^+ (totally positive classes in H^1(o_F[1/2], Z/2) ⊂ F^×/2) maps trivially to ℓ^×/2, and (iv) a Galois extension M ⊃ F of Q unramified at m such that for every p unramified, prime to 2ℓ and completely split in M, U_F^{(p+)} also maps trivially to ℓ^×/2.
contract.note: F = Q[x]/f for f = x^n + Σa_i x^{n−i} ± ℓ with real roots, roots ≡ 1 (mod 8) in Q_2, a prescribed ℓ_0-adic factorization, discriminant prime to m and irreducible; λ_0 = (α) with α a square at the places above 2.

contract.name: Compatible systems on the Hilbert–Siegel variety
contract.statement: For each place λ of F with residue characteristic prime to Δ, 𝒮[1/λ] carries the étale local system ρ_λ of o_{F,λ}-modules from the Tate module of the universal abelian scheme, pure of weight −1, coming over C from a local system of o_F-modules; at an F_q-point (q prime to Δ) the trace of Frobenius on ρ_λ lies in F and is independent of λ (Shimura, 11.10). The geometric image of ρ_λ is Sp_{2r}(o_{F,λ}) for λ ∤ e, and Zariski dense for λ | e.

contract.name: Vanishing of H^1 of the Hilbert–Siegel variety
contract.statement: H^1(S_C, ρ_λ) = 0; equivalently H^1(Γ, F^{2r} ⊗_ι C) = 0 for an arithmetic Γ ≤ Sp_{2r}(F) and each embedding ι : F → C.
contract.note: The paper sketches this from superrigidity or the congruence subgroup property ([F:Q] ≥ 3 gives real rank ≥ 3).

contract.name: Lemma 6.3.1: α_C = 0
contract.statement: Let α ∈ H^3_et(𝒮, ℓ^×/2) be the pullback of c_et along the reduction of ρ_{λ_0} (a GSp_{2r}(ℓ)-local system). Its restriction to S_C is trivial.
contract.note: Over C the local system lifts to Sp_{2r}(o_F); c_et then factors through U_F, landing in U_F^+ by the vanishing of c_31 on Sp_{2r}(R), and U_F^+ → ℓ^×/2 is trivial by §6.1 (iii).

contract.name: Lemma 6.3.2: killing α on special fibres
contract.statement: There is a finite Galois extension M/Q, unramified outside 2Δ (so at m), such that Frob_k trivial in Gal(M/Q) implies α_k = 0.
contract.note: Rπ_*(Z/2) on Z[1/Δ] has lcc cohomology sheaves (via the normal crossings compactification, SGA 4½ 'Théorèmes de finitude', appendix); M is the maximal exponent-2 abelian extension, unramified outside 2Δ, of the splitting field of H^2(S_Q̄, Z/2).

contract.name: Slicing down to a surface
contract.statement: For a geometrically irreducible component S° ⊂ P^m_{M_0} (M_0 = Q(ζ_e)) of dimension ≥ 3 whose boundary in its closure has codimension ≥ 3, a general M_0-rational hyperplane section is smooth, geometrically irreducible, has boundary codimension ≥ 3, and induces an isomorphism on π_1 of the complex points (Goresky–MacPherson, Stratified Morse Theory II.1.1), hence on H^1(−, ρ_λ). Iterating, one reaches a smooth projective surface with the same properties (a)–(d) of §6.4, which spread out over o_{M_0}[1/S] and specialize to F_p for large p split in M_0 (geometric monodromy preserved by SGA 1 X; H^1 = 0 by proper smooth base change).

contract.name: Guralnick–Tiep: the eighth-moment criterion for SO
contract.statement: For a reductive algebraic subgroup Γ ⊂ O(W), W orthogonal over a field of characteristic zero (of large enough dimension), dim(W^{⊗8})^Γ = dim(W^{⊗8})^{SO(W)} = C_4 = 8!/(4!·2^4) implies Γ ⊃ SO(W) (Guralnick–Tiep, Thm. 1.4).

contract.name: Lemma 6.4.2: points impose independent conditions on hypersurfaces
contract.statement: For pairwise distinct x_1, …, x_r in S°(F_q) and D ≥ r − 1, vanishing at all x_i is a codimension-r condition on Γ(S°_{F_q}, 𝒪(D)) (Poonen, Lemma 2.1), so the fraction of degree-D slices through them is (q^{E−r} − 1)/(q^E − 1) = q^{−r}(1 + O(q^{r−E})), E = dim Γ(S°, 𝒪(D)).
contract.note: Stated as corrected: the paper's choice of D does not guarantee D ≥ r − 1 (sourceIssues E8).

contract.name: Lemma 6.4.1: slices with nonvanishing central value
contract.statement: There are D_0 and p_0(D) such that for D ≥ D_0 and p ≥ p_0(D) split in M_0, the orthogonal local system 𝖶 (fibre H^1(X_h, ρ_λ)(−1)) on the space ℋ_D of smooth degree-D slices of the surface S°_{F_p} has geometric monodromy Zariski dense in SO; and there are an odd j and h ∈ ℋ_D(F_{p^j}) with slice X = X_h a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve such that (i) L(X, ρ_λ, 1) ≠ 0, (ii) the geometric monodromy of (X, ρ_λ) equals that of (S°, ρ_λ), (iii) j is odd.
contract.note: Method of moments: the eighth moment of the Frobenius traces on H^1(X_h, ρ_λ) over ℋ_D is bounded by C_4 q^4(1 + o(1)) using Lemma 6.4.2, Deligne's bound (6.15) and a Möbius inversion over set partitions; then Guralnick–Tiep and Chebotarev. (ii) is Grothendieck's Lefschetz theorem (SGA 2 XII Cor. 3.5).

contract.name: Lemma 6.5.1: c_et of the slices
contract.statement: There is a Galois extension M_1/Q, unramified at m, such that for the slices (X, ρ) of Lemma 6.4.1 (ρ the reduction of ρ_{λ_0}), c_et(X, ρ) is trivial whenever p is split in M_1.
contract.note: The printed statement says 'unramified outside m' (sourceIssues E11).

contract.name: Lemma 6.5.2: L-value of the slices
contract.statement: There is a Galois extension M_2/Q, unramified at m, such that L(X, ρ) is trivial whenever p is split in M_2 and sufficiently large: L(X, ρ_·, 1) ∈ F^× is totally positive (Riemann hypothesis) with even valuation at every λ ∤ 2p (Lemma 3.9.1), so its class lies in U_F^{(p+)}, which maps trivially to ℓ^×/2 by §6.1 (iv).

contract.name: c_et on the quaternion group
contract.statement: The pullback of the étale Chern class from H^3(SL_2(Q(i)), Q(i)^×/2) to Q_8 (Pauli matrices) is the unique nonzero class of H^3(Q_8, Z/2), valued in the subgroup generated by i: for q ≡ 5 (mod 8), Q_8 is a 2-Sylow subgroup of SL_2(F_q) and H_3(Q_8) → H_3(SL_2(F_q)) is onto, while i is a nonsquare in F_q.

contract.name: Both sides of Theorem 3.1 for quaternionic covers of curves
contract.statement: A Q_8-cover of a curve X/F_q is a quadratic étale X̃/X with involution σ and α : Pic(X̃) → Z/4 with σ^*α = −α and α|_{Pic X} the character of X̃/X (D.1). Then ∫_X of the generator of H^3(Q_8) equals y(ℒ_x), y ∈ H^1(X, Z/2) evaluated by class field theory on the 2-torsion bundle of x (Lemma D.4.1: ∫x² ∪ y = ∫β′(x) ∪ y, (D.2)); and L(X, ρ, 1/√q) = L(X̃, α, 1/√q) = Σ_k q^{−k/2}L_k with L_k = Σ_{deg D=k} α(D), symmetric under k ↔ 2g − 2 − k with sign α(𝒦). For genus-2 X : y² = xQ(x) with X̃ : w² = Q(t²) this gives qL(½, ρ) = 2q + Σ_{deg D=2} α(D) (D.6), and the invariant (D.5) vanishes iff (0) − (∞) ∈ π_*(ker α²).
contract.note: Several slips in D.2–D.6 are recorded as sourceIssues E22–E24.

contract.name: Numerical examples beyond the hypotheses of Theorem 3.1
contract.statement: Each of the hyperelliptic curves 2x⁸ + 2x⁶z² − 4x⁴z⁴ − 3x²z⁶ − 3z⁸ + y² = 0 over F_5, x⁸ + 4x⁶z² + 2x⁴z⁴ + 3x²z⁶ + 5z⁸ + y² = 0 over F_11, 5x⁸ + 2x⁶z² − 6x⁴z⁴ − 7x²z⁶ + 7z⁸ + y² = 0 over F_13 and 5x⁸ + 15x⁶z² + 15x⁴z⁴ + 2x²z⁶ + 12z⁸ + y² = 0 over F_17 carries a quaternionic local system with nonsquare qL(½) and nonvanishing invariant (D.5); in all computed examples 'qL(½) is a square' coincided with vanishing of (D.5).
contract.note: Recomputed independently (class groups and all 8 admissible α per curve): every nonzero qL(½) is ~ i and the pairing is nonzero; on the F_5 curve 4 of the 8 α have L(½) = 0, a case the paper does not discuss.
